300	def event_rungs(event, due_day, article_day):
   301	    """An event's rungs (D409): it happened; it is ruled out; neither. The model writes the first condition and, when something
   302	    can rule the event out before the due day, the way it names for that. Code writes the rest, so that exactly one rung holds
   303	    for every outcome whatever the two conditions say. The second rung takes the way the model names and every other decision
   304	    against the event as a whole, or abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole, and asks of each of them, the model's own
   305	    included, that it was made after the article's day and stands on the due day: so a rejection the model did not name is
   306	    never counted as still open, and one that was lifted, that concerns only a part, or that was already in place when the
   307	    question opened, is not counted as a ruling out, whether or not the model's sentence says so. The second
   308	    rung holds only when the first does not, and the last rung is the complement of the others. The labels answer the question
   309	    as it is printed beside them: Yes and No, or Yes, Ruled out and Still open."""
   310	    happened = {'label': 'Yes', 'condition': event['happened']}
   311	    if event['ruled_out'] is None:
   312	        return [happened, {'label': 'No', 'condition': f'Rung 1 does not hold on {due_day}.'}]
   313	    ruled_out = ruling_out_of(event).rstrip()
   314	    return [happened,
   315	            {'label': 'Ruled out',
   316	             'condition': f"{ruled_out}{'' if ruled_out.endswith('.') else '.'} This rung holds when that, or any other decision against the event of "
   317	                          f'rung 1 as a whole, or a formal abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole, was made after {article_day} and '
   318	                          f'stands on {due_day}, and only when rung 1 does not.'},
   319	            {'label': 'Still open', 'condition': f'Neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds on {due_day}.'}]

item.text:
**No-go on the composite mappings.** The page should display the three stored outcomes, but “Still open” does not mean a neutral investment effect, and the current Idea planner interprets the event’s endpoints differently from the proposed calculation.

For a three-choice event, the stored order is **Yes, Ruled out, Still open**. The Idea planner sends the model the *first and last* choices and asks which end supports the idea. Those ends are therefore **Yes and Still open**, not Yes and Ruled out. Mapping Ruled out to −2 while treating the planner’s `last` as the opposite endpoint would give its direction a different meaning from the one it was asked to choose. [idea_composite.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/idea_composite.py:278), [composite.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/idea/composite.js:121)

“Still open = 0” also contributes a numerical zero to the weighted composite; it is not missing data. It could dilute other drivers and imply an event with no conclusion is neutral for the idea. Until an explicit, reviewed rule says what an unresolved event contributes, show the outcome faithfully and make the affected composite unavailable or explicitly exclude it with the coverage consequence visible. Do not silently renormalise weights. [composite.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/idea/composite.js:21)

A theme with `n/a` can have an ordered **quantity** axis without asserting that higher is good for the company. It is usable in a composite only if the plan explicitly relates an endpoint to the particular idea and the product accepts the resulting ordinal and equal-spacing assumptions. Hiding the score on the card does not remove those assumptions from the composite. The design should either establish and test that contract or keep such a composite unavailable pending the choice.

For the standalone chart, stored-order lanes with the **outcome names** are defensible, provided the title and colours do not suggest an investment score. Show the actual range labels for themes and use neutral styling. Also cover the clean system’s **two-choice events**: its writer produces Yes / No when nothing can rule an event out, so testing only three-choice events leaves part of the new path under the old inferred-tone rule. [ladder_step.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/ladder_step.py:300)

The reader table also needs the server-side Idea planner, the score-definition table and bootstrap’s score display, alongside the listed card, chart and composite. Test their behaviour for each shape, including an unavailable composite and an older production dataset. [thesis-detail.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/components/thesis-detail.js:297), [bootstrap.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/bootstrap.js:138)

The next design can still unblock the library first: render stored outcomes and ranges without invented direction, then separately decide and prove what each shape may contribute to an Idea. D397’s pending browser proof should follow on that page.

CONSENSUS: no, because the event composite assigns an unsupported meaning to “Still open” and conflicts with the planner’s actual endpoints.
